details: Ancient non-standard units (handspan/balisht, cubit, angula) varied between individuals, causing trade confusion.
International System of Units (SI units) established the Meter (m) as the standard unit of length.
Unit Conversions: 1 km = 1000 m; 1 m = 100 cm; 1 cm = 10 mm.
experiments_or_examples: Measuring desk length using different students' handspans vs. a standard meter ruler

details: Scale Placement: Align scale touching the object along its length.
Worn-out Zero: Start from a clear mark (e.g., 1.0 cm) and subtract it from the final reading.
Parallax Error: Viewing at an angle gives incorrect readings. Position eye directly vertically above the mark.
experiments_or_examples: Measuring pencil length with three different eye positions (vertical vs angular)

details: A rigid ruler cannot directly measure curves.
A flexible thread is placed along the curved contour, marked with knots, and then measured straight on a ruler.
experiments_or_examples: Measuring the perimeter of a leaf or curved line using thread and ruler

branches.theme: 5.3 Rest, Motion, and Types of Motion

sub_branches.concept: Rest vs Motion Relative to Reference Points
details: Rest: Object position does not change with time relative to surroundings.
Motion: Object position changes continuously with time relative to surroundings.
experiments_or_examples: Classroom board (rest) vs flying bird or passing car (motion)

details: Rectilinear Motion: Movement along a straight line path (e.g., march past of soldiers, falling stone).
Circular Motion: Movement along a circular path maintaining fixed radius from center (e.g., fan blades, clock hands).
Periodic Motion: Motion repeating itself at regular fixed time intervals (e.g., swinging pendulum, child on swing).
Multiple Motions: Objects executing more than one motion type simultaneously (e.g., rolling wheel = circular + rectilinear).
experiments_or_examples: Dropping an eraser vertically (rectilinear); swinging a pendulum (periodic); spinning a top (circular)
